stem: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
solution: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, now observed as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas).

stem: The Constitution of India came into force on:
solution: The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

stem: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was:
solution: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is regarded as the chief architect of the Constitution.

stem: The introductory statement of the Constitution, setting out its ideals and objectives, is called the:
solution: The Preamble is the opening statement that lays out the guiding values and objectives of the Constitution.

stem: According to the Preamble, India is a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic:
solution: The Preamble declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

stem: The body that drafted the Constitution of India was the:
solution: The Constituent Assembly, whose members were chosen by the provincial assemblies, drafted the Constitution.

stem: The rights guaranteed to all citizens, which are protected by the Constitution, are called:
solution: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights guaranteed to citizens (e.g. equality, freedom) and are enforceable by the courts.

stem: The Indian Constitution is notable for being:
options: The shortest constitution in the world
One of the longest written constitutions in the world
solution: The Constitution of India is one of the longest and most detailed written constitutions in the world.

stem: A 'constitution' is best described as:
options: A set of basic rules and principles by which a country is governed
solution: A CONSTITUTION is the SET of BASIC RULES and PRINCIPLES by which a country is GOVERNED — its supreme law. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Constitution of India came into effect on:
solution: The Constitution came into EFFECT on 26 JANUARY 1950, celebrated as REPUBLIC DAY. (It was adopted on 26 November 1949.) So option 2 is correct.

stem: The date 26 January is celebrated every year as:
solution: 26 JANUARY, when the Constitution came into force, is celebrated as REPUBLIC DAY. So option 2 is correct.

stem: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
solution: The Constituent Assembly ADOPTED the Constitution on 26 NOVEMBER 1949; it came into effect on 26 January 1950. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution was:
solution: Dr B. R. AMBEDKAR was the CHAIRMAN of the DRAFTING COMMITTEE and is often called the chief architect of the Constitution. So option 2 is correct.

stem: The President of the Constituent Assembly was:
solution: Dr RAJENDRA PRASAD was the PRESIDENT of the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The introductory statement of the Constitution that lays out its ideals and objectives is called the:
solution: The PREAMBLE is the INTRODUCTORY statement laying out the IDEALS and OBJECTIVES of the Constitution. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Preamble describes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic:
solution: The Preamble declares India a SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'Sovereign' in the Preamble means that India:
options: Is free to take its own decisions, internal and external, without outside control
solution: SOVEREIGN means India is FREE to take its OWN DECISIONS, both INTERNAL and EXTERNAL, WITHOUT any OUTSIDE CONTROL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'Secular' in the Indian context means that:
options: The state treats all religions equally and has no official state religion
solution: SECULAR means the STATE treats ALL RELIGIONS EQUALLY and has NO OFFICIAL state religion, giving citizens freedom of religion. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. 'Republic' means the head of state is elected, not hereditary. 2. 'Democratic' means the government is elected by the people. Which is/are correct?
solution: BOTH are correct: REPUBLIC → head of state is ELECTED, not hereditary; DEMOCRATIC → government is ELECTED by the PEOPLE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Match List-I (Term in Preamble) with List-II (Meaning): P. Sovereign Q. Secular R. Republic S. Democratic | 1. Elected head of state 2. Independent in decisions 3. Elected by the people 4. Equal treatment of all religions
solution: Sovereign → independent in decisions (P-2); Secular → equal treatment of all religions (Q-4); Republic → elected head of state (R-1); Democratic → elected by the people (S-3). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Fundamental Rights are important because they:
options: Guarantee basic freedoms and can be enforced through the courts
Are only suggestions with no legal force
Can be freely denied to citizens
solution: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS GUARANTEE basic FREEDOMS and are ENFORCEABLE through the COURTS if violated. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a Fundamental Right guaranteed by the Constitution?
solution: The RIGHT to EQUALITY is a FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT (along with freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural/educational rights, and constitutional remedies). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'Directive Principles of State Policy' are:
options: Guidelines for the government to work toward social and economic welfare, though not enforceable in court
solution: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES are GUIDELINES for the GOVERNMENT to promote SOCIAL and ECONOMIC WELFARE; they are NOT ENFORCEABLE in court but are fundamental to governance. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The duties expected of every citizen, added to the Constitution, are called:
solution: The DUTIES expected of every citizen (e.g., respect the Constitution, protect the environment) are the FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights to citizens. Reason (R): These rights protect individuals from the misuse of power and ensure equality and freedom. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: these rights PROTECT individuals from MISUSE of POWER and ensure EQUALITY and FREEDOM. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why does India need a written constitution?
options: To lay down the framework of government, rights, and duties clearly for a large, diverse nation
To give power to a king
solution: A WRITTEN CONSTITUTION lays down the FRAMEWORK of GOVERNMENT, RIGHTS, and DUTIES CLEARLY, essential for a LARGE, DIVERSE nation like India. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Constitution divides government powers among:
options: The legislature, the executive, and the judiciary
solution: The Constitution divides powers among the LEGISLATURE (makes laws), the EXECUTIVE (implements them), and the JUDICIARY (interprets them). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Legislature — makes laws 2. Executive — implements laws 3. Judiciary — interprets laws and settles disputes. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: LEGISLATURE → makes laws; EXECUTIVE → implements laws; JUDICIARY → interprets laws and settles disputes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Constitution can be changed to meet new needs through the process of:
solution: The Constitution can be CHANGED through AMENDMENT, allowing it to adapt to NEW NEEDS over time. So option 1 is correct.

stem: That the Constitution can be amended shows it is:
options: A living document that can adapt over time
solution: The AMENDMENT provision shows the Constitution is a LIVING DOCUMENT that can ADAPT over TIME to changing circumstances. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Constitution establishes India as a 'federal' country, meaning power is shared between:
options: The central (Union) government and the state governments
solution: India is FEDERAL: power is SHARED between the CENTRAL (Union) government and the STATE governments. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The makers of the Constitution drew on ideas from many countries and India's own freedom struggle. Reason (R): They wanted to build a strong framework suited to India's needs and values. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the makers borrowed ideas from many countries and the freedom struggle. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: they did so to BUILD a STRONG FRAMEWORK SUITED to India's NEEDS and VALUES. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The phrase 'We, the people of India' in the Preamble emphasises that:
options: The Constitution derives its authority from the people of India
solution: 'WE, THE PEOPLE of INDIA' emphasises that the Constitution's AUTHORITY comes FROM the PEOPLE of India themselves. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The ideals of Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity are found in the:
solution: The ideals of JUSTICE, LIBERTY, EQUALITY, and FRATERNITY are enshrined in the PREAMBLE of the Constitution. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Fraternity' as an ideal in the Preamble means:
options: A sense of brotherhood and unity among all citizens
solution: FRATERNITY means a SENSE of BROTHERHOOD and UNITY among ALL CITIZENS, promoting the dignity of the individual and unity of the nation. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements about the Constitution is TRUE?
options: It is the supreme law, and all other laws must conform to it
solution: The Constitution is the SUPREME LAW; ALL OTHER LAWS must CONFORM to it. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Constitution took about how long to be prepared by the Constituent Assembly?
options: Almost 3 years (2 years, 11 months and 18 days)
solution: The Constituent Assembly took ALMOST 3 YEARS — precisely 2 years, 11 months and 18 days — to prepare the Constitution. So option 1 is correct.

stem: One key purpose of the Constitution is to protect citizens from:
options: The misuse of power by the government or any authority
solution: A KEY PURPOSE of the Constitution is to PROTECT citizens from the MISUSE of POWER by the government or any authority, through rights and rule of law. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which body has the power to interpret the Constitution and protect Fundamental Rights?
options: The judiciary (courts, especially the Supreme Court)
solution: The JUDICIARY — the COURTS, especially the SUPREME COURT — has the power to INTERPRET the Constitution and PROTECT Fundamental Rights. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The members of the Constituent Assembly were:
options: Chosen mainly by the provincial (elected) assemblies
solution: The members of the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY were CHOSEN mainly by the PROVINCIAL (elected) ASSEMBLIES, representing different regions and groups. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the ideals mentioned in the Preamble?
solution: MONARCHY is NOT a Preamble ideal. The Preamble upholds JUSTICE, LIBERTY, EQUALITY, and FRATERNITY. So option 3 is correct.

stem: 'Liberty' as an ideal in the Preamble refers to:
options: Freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
solution: LIBERTY in the Preamble refers to FREEDOM of THOUGHT, EXPRESSION, BELIEF, FAITH, and WORSHIP for citizens. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution guarantees the same Fundamental Rights to all citizens. 2. It allows the state to discriminate on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Which is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is TRUE — the same Fundamental Rights apply to ALL citizens. Statement 2 is FALSE — the Constitution PROHIBITS discrimination on those grounds. So only 1 is correct.

stem: The Right against Exploitation in the Constitution prohibits:
options: Forced labour, trafficking, and child labour in hazardous work
solution: The RIGHT against EXPLOITATION PROHIBITS FORCED LABOUR, TRAFFICKING, and CHILD LABOUR in hazardous work. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Constitution provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies. Reason (R): It allows citizens to approach the courts if their Fundamental Rights are violated. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Constitution gives the Right to CONSTITUTIONAL REMEDIES. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: it lets citizens APPROACH the COURTS when their FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS are VIOLATED (Dr Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is it said that the Constitution reflects the values of the freedom struggle?
options: It enshrines ideals like equality, liberty and justice that the freedom movement fought for
solution: The Constitution REFLECTS the FREEDOM STRUGGLE because it ENSHRINES the IDEALS — EQUALITY, LIBERTY, JUSTICE — that the movement fought for. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Fundamental Duties remind citizens that along with rights they also have:
options: Responsibilities toward the nation and fellow citizens
solution: FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES remind citizens that along with RIGHTS they have RESPONSIBILITIES toward the NATION and FELLOW CITIZENS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best explains why the Constitution is called the 'supreme law of the land'?
options: No law or action of government can violate it, and all must follow it
It is written in many languages
solution: The Constitution is SUPREME because NO LAW or GOVERNMENT ACTION can VIOLATE it, and ALL must FOLLOW it. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Studying the Constitution helps citizens to:
options: Understand their rights and duties and participate meaningfully in democracy
solution: Studying the Constitution helps citizens UNDERSTAND their RIGHTS and DUTIES and PARTICIPATE meaningfully in DEMOCRACY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'The Constitution of India — An Introduction' is that:
options: The Constitution of India, drafted by the Constituent Assembly and in force from 26 January 1950, is the supreme written law that lays out the ideals in its Preamble, guarantees Fundamental Rights, sets Directive Principles and Duties, divides power among organs of government, and can be amended — providing the framework for India to function as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic
solution: The OVERALL MESSAGE is that the CONSTITUTION of INDIA — drafted by the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY and in force from 26 JANUARY 1950 — is the SUPREME WRITTEN LAW. It lays out IDEALS in its PREAMBLE, guarantees FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, sets DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES and DUTIES, DIVIDES POWER among the organs of government, and can be AMENDED, providing the framework for India as a SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC. So option 2 is correct.
